Published Sep 13, 2026, 12:55 PM EDT

Zoë Miskelly is an editor and second in command for Screen Rant's Movies team, having covered the entertainment industry for almost 10 years now. Zoë's love of superheroes and all things Marvel & DC started out in childhood, and has blossomed into a career getting to talk about some of the biggest and best movies and shows of all time, having previously focused on comics while working at WhatCulture.

The MCU's plans for Spider-Man 5 mark a major milestone for the franchise in terms of a movie first, painting a promising picture of what's to come for the Marvel movie empire. As the MCU timeline approaches entering into its second decade - with Iron Man having debuted in 2008 - the way the franchise intends to continue on in terms of the big picture seems all the more important.

It's clear the MCU has the capacity to continue on for many years to come, and the MCU audience's positive reception of characters like Tom Holland's Spider-Man provides a solid way for the franchise to stick the landing in terms of setting itself up for many more decades down the line, by showing that the MCU can provide consistent and engaging stories.

The teased plans for Spider-Man 5 following the success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day certainly seem to be in line with this, especially since the movie would currently break a major milestone for the MCU overall. Thankfully, this milestone is one that Spider-Man 5 seems almost custom-built to handle well and in a way that enhances the overall MCU and its long-term plans, so long as the fifth Spider-Man installment does indeed come to fruition.

Spider-Man 5 Will Be The First Time A Solo Marvel Hero Gets A Five-Movie-Long MCU Series

Credit: Sony Pictures Releasing

With the latest update about Spider-Man 5 being Sony Pictures chairman and CEO Ravi Ahuja stating that “We don’t have a date for it yet." regarding when the movie might release, it seems as though there are definite plans for the MCU Spider-Man movie series to continue forward, which seems par for the course given Spider-Man: Brand New Day's $2.4B box office results at this point in time.

This is exciting in terms of following up on the story of Brand New Day, which set up a promising new era for the web-slinging hero, but is also interesting in terms of what it means for the MCU more broadly speaking.

The release of Spider-Man 5 would mean the series is the MCU's first to reach five films while centering primarily on one lone hero, unless Peter is beaten to the punch - but given the more divided reception to the fourth Thor movie and the fourth Captain America movie being Sam Wilson's first movie appearance in this hero mantle, it does seem that Spider-Man will be the first to reach this major MCU milestone.

Spider-Man 5 Being The First To Break This MCU Record Makes Perfect Sense For The Franchise

Ultimately, the box office success of the MCU Spider-Man series has been the franchise's strongest outside of the Avengers series itself. Spider-Man: Brand New Day displays this strikingly well, with its $2.4 billion box office being some of the highest results in the entire MCU other than Avengers: Endgame.

The colossal level of interest in Spider-Man's MCU story that this reflects means it would seem almost surreal to not go forward with Spider-Man 5 and possibly an entire second trilogy for Tom Holland's Peter Parker, especially since the critical reception to Spider-Man: Brand New Day has also been decidedly positive, with fans eager to see the hero grow up and evolve on-screen following his origin story trilogy of sorts.

As the MCU continues, it seems more and more viable for heroes and solo series to reach their fifth installment, and Spider-Man 5 is arguably the perfect way to test these waters, by breaking this milestone with Marvel's biggest hero, and a character who MCU audiences in particular seem eager to see appear on the big screen in yet another chapter of his personal life story.
